messages:
From: Aisha Patterson <aisha.patterson@aurora-apps.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora SRE <sre@aurora-apps.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors & latency spike - urgent

Jonas —

We started seeing a significant increase in 5xx errors and tail latency in production around 08:35 PT. Error rate jumped to ~6% for inference routes that touch the personalization cache and throughput dropped by ~40%. Our customer-facing pages are timing out for ~10% of users.

I’ve attached the initial error dump and a screenshot of our dashboard. Can you confirm receipt and whether you have a mitigation plan? We need an ETA for resolution and whether we should failover traffic to another region or model variant.

Aisha
Aisha Patterson
Head of Platform — Aurora Apps

Attachments: aura_error_log_20261019.txt, throughput_dashboard.png

Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike - urgent

Aisha —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. We’ve stood up a short "command-post" to triage — looping in our SRE and exec leads. Immediate plan: 1) isolate the impacted routes, 2) enable model-variant fallback for heavy personalization requests, 3) apply temporary client-side throttling for non-critical endpoints.

Can Aurora share the spike start time with exact request IDs if available (Samir/Rao)? We’ll confirm the mitigation steps in the next 20 minutes and post continuous updates to this thread and the shared drive link.

Proposed 30-min command-post at 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow). Please mark urgent.

— Jonas

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Aurora SRE <sre@aurora-apps.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production errors & latency spike - urgent

Quick triage summary:
- Symptoms: increased 5xx across personalization routes; sustained 95th/99th latency jump; KV cache miss ratio rose sharply at 08:34 PT.
- Root cause hypothesis: aggressive KV cache eviction combined with a sudden influx of heavy context requests (seq lengths >> baseline). This caused request queueing and led to worker OOMs on a subset of nodes.

Immediate actions I’ve executed (09:30 PT):
1) Bumped per-node max-conns and temporarily increased concurrency cap for dedicated pool to reduce queue head-of-line blocking.
2) Enabled a lighter model-variant (quantized) as fallback for personalization routes (will accept slightly lower quality but keeps latency within SLO).
3) Applied a short-lived request-rate limit for non-authenticated batch endpoints (5 min rolling).
4) Collected debug logs and uploaded to the shared drive (see link).

Next steps (owner):
- Evelyn: keep the fallback variant live and watch error rate for 15m windows.
- Jonas/Laura: coordinate customer comms and decide on credit/SLA messaging.
- Marcus: exec notification and decision on extended credits if outage persists >2 hrs.

I’ll update in 15 minutes with metrics.

Evelyn
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: aura_error_log_20261019.txt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patterson <aisha.patterson@aurora-apps.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@aurora-apps.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2026 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Aurora incident: immediate status and next steps

Aisha / Samir —

Post-triage update and next steps (we will continue to post updates to the shared drive):

Summary of impact:
- Window: 08:34 PT — ongoing (investigation continues).
- Error rate: peaked ~6% across personalization routes; currently down to ~1.2% after mitigations.
- Throughput: targeted routes saw ~35% throughput reduction at peak.

What we did (executed by 09:30 PT):
- Enabled quantized model fallback for heavy personalization routes.
- Increased per-node concurrency caps and drained/restarted 4 affected workers.
- Applied temporary rate-limiting on non-critical endpoints.

Customer-facing effect & mitigation plan:
- Immediate: Most user-facing pages should return to normal within 10–15 minutes barring residual queueing.
- Short term (0–2 hrs): We will keep the fallback variant active and gradually ramp primary variant back while monitoring 1m/5m error windows.
- If errors remain >1% after 2 hrs: will open a post-mortem and propose a service credit (prelim approval discussed internally).

ETA: We expect error rate to return under 0.5% within 45 minutes; we will send a follow-up at 11:00 PT with updated metrics.

Attachments: SLA overview for Aurora (sla-overview-Aurora.pdf).

If you want us to fail traffic to a different region or to a warmed standby, please say so and we’ll proceed.

Best —
Jonas Weber
Director, Technical Sales — Redwood Inference
